elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "TrueLink shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client and its affiliates..." — express "defend" verb naming Client and affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...hold harmless Client and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)..."

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): "an allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services or the Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — captures the offerings supplied under this Agreement (no separate deliverables construct appears).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or Credit Data caused by TrueLink" — Vendor-caused breach of the Agreement's data categories is covered.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (iv): "TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct" (US spelling of "wilful").

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Revised §12a now reads only: "(i) any claim arising out of or relating to the Client Content, and (ii) any violation by Client of any applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation"; the former breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default, Web Site and product-liability limbs are struck.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted limb (i) covering infringement/misappropriation of any intellectual property right by the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; condition does not apply because the drafter included no exclusions, leaving the indemnity broader (more favourable to Client).

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination carve-out was added, so nothing narrows the indemnity against Client.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification carve-out appears, which is acceptable and favourable to Client.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy obligation; nothing elsewhere in §12 supplies one.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic is drafted for the case where alternative remedies are unavailable.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual fees super-cap is stated; the drafter deliberately did not volunteer one at the preferred level.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete: the inserted TrueLink paragraph delivers defend + indemnify for Client and affiliates against third-party claims across all four required subject-matter limbs (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access/disclosure, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and carries the full notice / control-of-defence / reasonable-cooperation procedure in operative text, not merely in the comment.

Customer-side narrowing is done in operative language: §12a is cut back to Client Content and Client's violation of applicable law, removing the breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default, Web Site and product-liability limbs, exactly as the tenth preferred element requires.

Fallback level is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace, no refund fallback, no 3× super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is fully met; the drafter correctly declined to volunteer a super-cap.

Minimality holds: a concise insertion for a missing clause plus the required narrowing of §12a, with no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no extra damages categories and no super-cap or other off-checklist requirement. The favourable existing TrueLink indemnity in §12b for breach/non-performance is retained untouched.
Intent preserved: the new procedure sentence applies even-handedly across Section 12 without contradicting the retained §12b, and no cross-reference is left dangling by the deletions in §12a.

Housekeeping (not a defect on the record before me): confirm that "Client Content" and "Credit Data" are defined terms in the Agreement and that together they capture all data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Client; if any Client data category falls outside both, broaden limb (iii) to "Client Content, Credit Data or any other data of or relating to Client" so the data-breach trigger is not limited to selected named data types.
